_README: THE AUTHORITY for what the artifact manifest digests. Committed, closed, and bound to the deployed
commit through L2: the verifier loads this file from the exported release, and its authority comes
from L2 having proven that blob equal to the commit tree in the object store -- not from the file
The receipt RECORDS the exclusion list and this file's digest for auditability, and may never define
them. A receipt that could name its own exclusions could exempt node_modules and then verify itself,
which is the circularity this file exists to break.
WHAT IS DIGESTED: every behaviour-bearing byte in the release -- the exported source, next-env.d.ts,
.next/** and node_modules/** INCLUDING every native .node. Excluding node_modules was a real defect:
the two files that prove which release a worker loaded are better_sqlite3.node and next-swc, both of
which live there, so excluding it would have excluded the only native code in the process.
SHARED SYMLINK TARGETS are not listed below and must never be. They are excluded BEHAVIOURALLY: the
walker records a link by its target text and never follows it, so no .env line and no database byte
can enter the manifest. Adding them here would imply the walker had looked.
If the verifier cannot load this policy, the result is `unverified`. It has no built-in defaults, on
purpose: a verifier with defaults passes when its policy is missing.

exclusions.detail: Next's own runtime cache (ISR, fetch, image optimizer). Measured on release 20260824_134957 as three files last written inside the build window, with no runtime write in the following 5h45m -- but it is the location Next writes to at runtime, so it is excluded on principle rather than on that observation.
Build profiling output written as the build completes. Carries no behaviour.
Build profiling output written as the build completes. Carries no behaviour.
Build telemetry written at build completion. Carries no behaviour.

The provenance stamp, written BEFORE the build so an aborted build still leaves an identifiable directory. That ordering is exactly why it cannot carry a digest of the build output, and why the receipt is a separate post-build file.
The receipt cannot digest itself: its own manifest_digest field is not known until the digest is computed.
